messages.subject: FW: [DIST-SAMP] Solutions to: Internal Error 457, Error 91 and Error about effort
parts:
Hi list

I came across Anna's summary below after getting the internal
error 457 when trying to use MRDS in Distance 6.2.

However, my solution differed to that offered by Eric & I'm writing to the
list to see whether it's OK or not. To recap, Eric's solution was to
create an additional field 'Observer' populated with '1' for all
detections.

My solution is different. I realised that with my current dataset, I
already have a field 'Observer'. No prizes for guessing what sort of
information is already in it! So I simply renamed this to 'Person' and
re-ran the analysis with settings as 'ds - single observer'. It worked,
giving results close to CDS with the same model.

My question is: is this OK or should I have implemented Eric's solution?

Looking at the logs from R, the following warnings came up:

Warning messages:
1: In `$.data.frame`(region.table, Region) :
Name partially matched in data frame
2: In `$.data.frame`(region.table, Region) :
Name partially matched in data frame

Thanks,


Stewart

>>line transect based survey (single observer).

>>Problem 1: Internal Error 457: "This key is already associated with an
>>element of this collection"
>>
>>I managed to get abundance and density estimates which seem accurate
>>easily
>>using CDS analysis without any errors. However when trying to the MRDS
>>engine it wouldn't run either half normal or hazard rate analysis due to
>>Internal Error 457.
>>
>>
>>
>>Solution: The MDRS engine wants to work with double observer data, and
>>even
>>though you can trick it into using single observer data the settings for
>>the
>>survey type must be set to double observer and have a field 'Observer'
>>which
>>would contain '1' for all detections.
>>
>>
>>
>>Problem 2: **Error: The layer 'Line transect' specified by the Survey
>>for
>>calculating efforts is higher than the sample layer specified in the
>>Model
>>Definition.
>>Correct effort values can therefore not be calculated.**
>>
>>
>>
>>Solution: Change the survey properties. Visit the Surveys Tab,
>>Properties
>>button, Data fields tab and change the Effort Role to which ever layer
>>contains the Effort (for me the Segment layer).
>>
>>If you look at the Dolphin.dst example, the effort is to be defined at
>>the
>>segment (subsample1) layer of your project with a field found there.
>>This
>>is different to the way in which "normal" distance sampling works
>>wherein
>>we
>>are interested in the lengths of various segments. With DSM, the
>>modelling
>>is taking place at the level of the transect segments, so Distance needs
>>to
>>know the size of the segments (defined using the field called 'Effort')
>>that
>>contains the length of each segment.
>>
>>Problem 3: Error 91: **Error Unexpected error** "Object variable or With
>>block variable not set". - in the DSM analysis
>>
>>
>>
>>Solution: The problem was as simple as rerunning the detection function
>>fitting analyses after you had changed the Analysis preferences such that
>>the objects were not erased after their creation. I suspect you had run
>>analysis 1, then reset the preferences such that analysis 1 R results
>>were
>>retained, then run your dsm analysis that complained that the analysis 1
>>results could not be found.
>>
>>
>>
>>I hope this helps anyone having a simlar issues and thanks again to Eric

messages.author: 350dad0a615d36db
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] FW: [DIST-SAMP] Solutions to: Internal Error 457, Error 91 and Error about effort
parts:
Hi Stewart and list,

mrds does expect an "observer" column in the data. The "partially
matched" warning means that R means that you have some other column in
your data with a title that starts "observer" and R has partially
matched the name (this is an R feature, so you can write "data$longvar"
and get the contents of "data$longvariablenamethatidontwanttotype").

So, in your case you might still have the wrong data in your model
(though if the results are close, perhaps not). It's safest to create
that extra column of all 1s to ensure that mrds is interpreting the data
as single observer.


Hope this helps.

best,
--dave

parts:
Dear listfolk,

Stewart wrote back to ask a further question, which I thought may be
pertinent to those of you using mrds within Distance.

Stewart writes:

""
In reply to your and Eric's answers (below) I'm trying to do the right
thing now with respect to MRDS, so I've included a data column
'observer' populated with '1's after setting up a new project as double
observer. However, I get an error when trying to run MRDS:

[Observation].[Perp distance] AS distance
[Observation].[object] AS object
[Observation].[observer] AS observer
[Observation].[detected] AS detected
[Observation].[species] AS species
[Observation].[person] AS person
[Observation].[burnt] AS burnt
[Line transect].[Label] AS label
[Line transect].[Line length] AS line.length
[Region].[Label] AS stratum.label
[Region].[Area] AS area
[Study area].[Label] AS global.label


**Error: Some values in the object field are not unique**

I didn't include a field called 'object' or 'detected' but it seems to
be trying to match it to my data.

I had a look at the help file and it seems that I may need to create
another two columns 'object' and 'detected' but this seems to be a bit
more than was suggested by yourself and Eric in previous answers. Is
this the case?
""

Indeed, Stewart is correct. Data for mrds require "object" and
"detected" columns. The object field should be unique to each
observation (so there should only be duplicated object IDs if you have a
double observer study) and the detected should be 1 if the object was
detected (again, 0s only occur in double observer surveys).

Further information can be found in the "Details" section of the ddf
section of the mrds R package manual
http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/mrds/mrds.pdf


I hope this is helpful!

best,
--dave
